question: Till 20 January 1972, which present-day Indian state was known as the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** was known as the **North-East Frontier Agency** (NEFA) during **British India** and the **Republic of India until 1972**.

 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh **was initially a** Union Territory** that was **carved out **of **Assam**.
 
• On** 15th August 1947** when India became an independent nation, **North East Frontier Agency** commonly known as NEFA became an **integral part **of the **Union **of **India**.
 
• It was **administrated **by the** Ministry of External Affairs** with the** Governor of Assam **acting as an **agent **to the **President **of **India**. 
 
• The language ‘Idu Mishmi’ is spoken in the state of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The capital of Arunachal Pradesh is Itanagar.
 
• State bird: Great hornbill.
 
• State flower: Fox-tail Orchid
 
• State tree: Hollong.
 
• State animal: Mithun (also known as Gayal).
